narrative.overview:
The website uses the app's design system rather than a brand of its own. OpenFishing is a tackle box: dark, ordered compartments where every lure has its numbered slot and its record. The world is the water at dusk. Deep, cool surfaces step up in small tonal increments, and a single cyan accent glints against them like a lure catching the last light. Real photos of lures and catches (here, real demo screenshots) carry the color, and the interface around them stays quiet and in order.

The app's direction is catalogued, built for outdoors: precise, inventory-like detail (numbered plates, mono spec values) plus legibility that survives glare. The website carries that over to a Persuade surface. Its job is to get an angler into the live demo, so it is allowed things the app is not: larger marketing type, one hero, generous section spacing. Every token, font, radius and rule below otherwise comes from the app. The app's DESIGN.md (github.com/m1ndgames/OpenFishing/blob/main/DESIGN.md) is the upstream authority. When the two disagree, the app wins and this file is updated.

The site's one addition with no counterpart in the app is the lure-and-fish background animation on the landing page, kept as the website's single moment of play.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, tonal layering; light mode is a fully designed counterpart, not an inversion.
One accent (Ocean cyan), used for actions, active state and the lure number, never as decoration.
DM Sans for everything readable; JetBrains Mono only for catalogued numbers and shell commands.
Flat surfaces with 1px borders; shadows only on floating layers and as a hover response.
Gently curved, consistent corners (9px controls, 14px cards).
Real product imagery (demo screenshots) does the persuading; the chrome stays quiet.

rules.name: The Single Glint Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue. It marks what you can act on and what is selected, and nothing else. Semantic colors are not accents and are never decorative.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components take every color from `--of-*` tokens, never literals. The one exception is the fixed photo scrim behind badges that sit on screenshots.

rules.name: The Upstream Rule
rules.body: Token values are changed in the app first. The website mirrors them; it never forks them.

rules.name: The Glare Rule
rules.body: Anything a visitor needs to read uses `--of-text-2` (`mist`) or brighter. `fog` is for hints and inactive states only.

rules.name: The Stencil Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for catalogued numbers and literal commands. Never use it for prose, labels, headings or tech-stack chips.

rules.name: The Long-Word Rule
rules.body: Every label must survive German and Polish string lengths. Allow wrapping in buttons and chips, and never put a fixed width on text-bearing controls.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: DM Sans carries every heading, from the hero down. There is no second display face.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels never carry a shadow at rest.

dos: Do take every color from an `--of-*` token, mirrored from the app.
Do check every change in dark and light mode at WCAG AA (`scripts/a11y.mjs`).
Do keep one solid-accent primary action per view, and make it the demo.
Do use JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals for lure numbers and counts, and for literal commands; nowhere else.
Do keep cards flat at rest (14px radius, 1px faint border).
Do show the real product (demo screenshots) rather than illustrations.
Do keep the wordmark and mark SVGs as they are, colored by `currentColor` from the accent.
donts: Don't reintroduce Carter One or any second display face.
Don't use `fog` (`--of-text-4`) for anything a visitor needs to read.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or use semantic red/green/amber decoratively.
Don't drift toward generic SaaS: no gradient blobs, purple or multi-hue gradients, or stock startup illustrations.
Don't tip into cartoonish: the fish animation is the whole play allowance; no clip-art, mascots or bouncy decoration.
Don't crowd the page like a bait-shop flyer: no stacked banners, loud badges or competing CTAs.
Don't set text below 0.75rem, or give text-bearing controls fixed widths.
Don't fork token values from the app.
